findings.title: redactPaths misses absolute paths adjacent to Markdown punctuation ([, |, <, *) and file:// URIs, so served task/prompt text can carry them
findings.evidence: `redactPaths` (server/projects.ts:53-55) only redacts a path when it is at the start of the string or preceded by one of `\s " ' ` ( = : ; ,`. The new run-inputs payload serves large operator-authored Markdown (`task.text`, `prompt.text`) through `boundedText` (server/projects.ts:370-377, used at 426-427), which relies solely on this regex. Probe against the real app (scratchpad/probe-adapter.mts): a ui task `Read [<root>/x/y](<root>/x/y) and |<root>/x/y| and file://<root>/x/y and <<root>/x/y> and *<root>/x/y* first.` was served by GET .../inputs as `Read [/tmp/probe-99GzsY/x/y](<path>) and |/tmp/probe-99GzsY/x/y| and file:///tmp/probe-99GzsY/x/y and </tmp/probe-99GzsY/x/y> and */tmp/probe-99GzsY/x/y* first.` (response body contained the temp root). The same regex guards finding messages/requirements (server/projects.ts:404-405) and completion/handoff summaries (438-439).
findings.failure: A pinned task or recorded prompt that names an absolute path inside a Markdown link label `[/home/u/repo/x]`, table cell `|/home/u/x|`, angle-bracket autolink `</home/u/x>`, emphasis `*/home/u/x*`, or a `file:///home/u/x` URI is returned verbatim by GET .../runs/{run}/inputs (and the same spellings in a finding message by .../reviews/{attempt}), violating the PRD rule that absolute paths pass through redaction and the `paths-redacted`/`inputs-paths-redacted` acceptance scenarios.
findings.fix: Replace the positive lookbehind allowlist with a negative lookbehind on path characters (e.g. `(?<![A-Za-z0-9._@~+-])`) so any non-path delimiter counts, and add an explicit alternative for `file://` prefixes; extend the redaction test in server/projects.test.ts with these spellings.

findings.title: requirement_found_in is computed on the full raw task, but the served task.text is truncated at 65536 chars, so a finding can claim a verbatim match the client cannot find
findings.evidence: `lanesQuoting` (server/projects.ts:387-395) tests `worker.task.includes(requirement)` on the untruncated section text, while `projectInputs` serves `task: boundedText(worker.task)` (line 426) which cuts at TEXT_LIMIT=65536 (lines 370-377). Probe (scratchpad/probe-adapter.mts): a ui task of 70000 'x' characters followed by the quote `Render the verdict pill on the review node.` and a finding quoting it: GET .../reviews/1 returned `requirement_found_in: ["ui"]`, GET .../inputs returned `task.truncated: true` and `task.text.includes(quote) === false`. The contract README defines the field as "the worker lanes whose task text contains the quote verbatim" and the UI (src/projects/WorkerInputs.tsx:60) then shows "The quoted requirement was not found in this task text" after following the link.
findings.failure: For any run whose pinned task exceeds 65536 characters (redacted length) with a reviewer quote located past the cut, the review payload links the finding to the lane while the inputs payload the viewer uses for highlighting does not contain the quote; the finding-to-task link lands on a task panel that says the quote was not found.
findings.fix: Compute the match against the same bounded text that is served (redact, truncate, then search for the redacted quote), or, if raw matching is kept deliberately, only report a lane when the quote also survives in the served `task.text`; add a test with a quote beyond TEXT_LIMIT.

findings.title: Check/scenario ids valid under the policy schema (any non-empty string) fail the strict inputs section, and one such run makes the whole workflow run list a 500
findings.evidence: `workerInputSchema.checks[].id` and `scenarios[].id` use `id = z.string().regex(ID_PATTERN)` (server/projects.ts:58, 94-99), whereas the producer's policy schema only requires `minLength: 1` for both (contracts/workflow/verification.schema.json `workers.items.properties.checks.items.properties.id` and `scenarios.items.properties.id`), and `validate_policy` adds no pattern check. `export_state.inputs_section` copies the ids verbatim (workflow/export_state.py:124-126). `listRuns` projects every run eagerly and throws on the first invalid one (server/projects.ts:540-541, 650-651). Probe (scratchpad/probe-adapter.mts): a run with check id `unit tests` beside a healthy run: GET .../runs → 500 RUN_STORAGE_INVALID `run-state.json inputs.workers.ui.checks.0.id: Invalid string: must match pattern ...`, while GET .../runs/ok-run → 200.
findings.failure: A policy.json with a check id such as `unit tests`, `e2e/smoke` or `-lint` (accepted by `workflow prepare`) produces a run that the controller exports normally; once that run exists, every run in the workflow disappears from the Projects viewer (list 500) although each sibling's detail still loads. Before this change the same policy was viewable because 1.0.0 exports carried no inputs section.
findings.fix: Either align the policy schema with ID_PATTERN so such policies are rejected at `prepare`, or degrade in the adapter: treat an inputs/review section that fails strict validation as "not recorded" for that run (404 INPUTS_NOT_FOUND / REVIEW_NOT_FOUND plus a warn) instead of failing the run and the list, so one run's section cannot hide the workflow; add a list-level test with a sibling run.

findings.title: Ctrl-C in the reviewer launch window (settle poll / pane attach) strands a live, fully identified reviewer with no resume or reconcile path
findings.evidence: `_review_native` wraps `runtime.launch_reviewer` in `except BaseException` and writes `automatic-review.json` as `needs_reconciliation` with `error: str(error)`; for KeyboardInterrupt that is the empty string. `InteractiveSessions.launch` (interactive.py:142) does the same to `review.interactive.json` even though `claude --bg` already exited 0 and the row is registered; `Pipeline.launch_reviewer` only catches `Exception` around the best-effort pane attach, so a Ctrl-C during `attach_reviewer_panel` also escapes as BaseException. `review_candidate` (automatic.py:242) then refuses forever, and the `reconcile` CLI action (pipeline.py:668-676) only handles `launch_*` steps, never the review node. Reproduced offline with the fixture (scratchpad/audit_experiments2.py `launch`): after `run_reviewer` succeeded and a KeyboardInterrupt followed, `review.interactive.json` = `attached_session_available` with session 3333…, `sessions.locate('review')` finds it, `automatic-review.json` = {status: needs_reconciliation, error: ''}, the checkpoint is clean (`next=('review',)`, no task error), yet the next `drive` raises 'Non-retryable graph failure' with the task error 'Prior reviewer invocation needs reconciliation'. No `review` event with status interrupted/blocked is emitted (timeline shows only 'Launching the native reviewer session'). By contrast an interrupt inside `wait_review` (the `wait` variant) resumes and completes. PRD_REVIEWER_PANE §5 requires 'Interrupting the supervisor during the review leaves the reviewer running and `automatic --live` resumes it'; RUNBOOK:235 tells the operator to 'start a new run for a fresh review'.
findings.failure: Operator presses Ctrl-C (or the SSH session drops) within the ~10-40 s after `claude --bg` returns while `settle('review')` polls for the PID or `require_shell` waits for the reviewer pane -> the reviewer session keeps running and consuming usage, `automatic --live` is refused on every attempt, the only documented recovery is a whole new run with a new bundle, and nothing in events.jsonl records the interruption or the live session id.
findings.fix: Treat a KeyboardInterrupt after `review.interactive.json` has a `session_id` (or after `run_reviewer` returned) like the wait interrupt: keep/put `automatic-review.json` at `running` with the session id from the native receipt, emit the `review`/`interrupted` resume note, and re-raise; catch BaseException (not just Exception) around the pane attach in `Pipeline.launch_reviewer`. Additionally let `review_candidate` reconcile a `needs_reconciliation` receipt through `sessions.run_reviewer`'s existing-receipt branch (which never relaunches) and continue into `_accept_native`, or expose a `reconcile` path for the review node; record a non-empty error (`repr(error)` or the exception class) so the receipt explains itself. Add a graph test for an interrupt raised from `run_reviewer`/pane attach asserting the resume completes with exactly one launch.

findings.title: A failed or interrupted stop after an accepted verdict is never retried: the run integrates with the reviewer still running and no event records the failed stop
findings.evidence: `_accept_native` marks the receipt `succeeded` (line 269, saved at 307) and only then calls `runtime.stop_reviewer()` at line 323, outside the try block: a RuntimeError from `stop_session` ('Stop failed for review' / 'termination is not established') or a KeyboardInterrupt propagates out of the review node with no `runtime.event`. On the next `drive`, `review_candidate`'s `succeeded` branch (236-238) returns the persisted review without looking at `review.stop.json`. Reproduced offline (scratchpad/audit_experiments.py experiment 1): with `stop_reviewer` failing once, the first drive ends in 'Non-retryable graph failure', `automatic-review.json` is `succeeded`, no `review.stop.json` exists, the review events are only running/interactive; the resumed `drive` raises the same error with 0 stop calls, an operator `retry` (`graph.invoke(None)`) integrates the candidate with 0 stop calls, and `sessions.locate('review')` still finds the live reviewer afterwards. The RUNBOOK (line 192) promises 'After acceptance or a block the controller stops the reviewer'.
findings.failure: `claude stop` returns non-zero once (or the PID lingers a moment, or Ctrl-C lands during the stop) after the verdict was accepted -> the run halts with a generic 'Non-retryable graph failure', the operator's `retry` fast-forwards the feature branch while the reviewer session is still alive and billable, `review.stop.json` never reaches `stopped: true`, and the timeline never says the stop failed.
findings.fix: Make the post-acceptance stop idempotent and re-entrant: in `review_candidate`'s `succeeded` branch call `runtime.stop_reviewer()` when `review.stop.json` is absent or `stopped` is false (the stop intent already makes a second call safe), and wrap the line-323 stop so a failure emits a `review`/`blocked` event ('Could not confirm reviewer stop: …') before re-raising. Add a graph test where `stop_reviewer` fails once and assert the resumed drive stops the reviewer before integrating.

findings.title: The post-wait identity, independence, worktree and evidence re-checks in `_accept_native` are not exercised by any test (PRD work item 5 requires the wrong-UUID case)
findings.evidence: `grep -n 'identity changed or is not independent\|Reviewer worktree changed\|Evidence changed during review\|Could not confirm reviewer stop' workflow/test_*.py` returns nothing. `FakeSessions.inventory`/`locate` (test_pipeline.py:69-84) always return the receipt's own UUID in state `idle`, so no graph test can make the located row differ from `automatic-review.json['session_id']` or equal a worker's session id; the `assert_rejected` family (test_automatic.py:535-572) only mutates the completion file (bundle hash, launch token, candidate, extra key, verdict, P1) and the print-mode fixture never reaches these lines. PRD_REVIEWER_PANE §4 item 5 lists 'a rejected completion file (wrong bundle hash, wrong UUID, wrong candidate) fails closed' and the design spec §3.3 requires the post-wait 'sessionId == receipt session_id and not equal to either worker session id' check; the handoff claims 'every rejected completion file' is tested.
findings.failure: A regression in the four lines (for example dropping the `in worker_ids` clause, or comparing against `review.interactive.json` instead of the bundle snapshots) would pass the whole offline suite while a reviewer that is actually one of the worker sessions, or a session swapped under the same background id, has its verdict accepted; the deadline/blocked paths that call `stop_reviewer` from the `except BaseException` branch are covered, but the branch's 'Could not confirm reviewer stop' fallback is not.
findings.fix: Give `FakeSessions` a hook (e.g. `reviewer_row_override`) so `inventory()` can report a different `sessionId` for the reviewer, or a worker's id, after launch; add graph tests asserting 'identity changed or is not independent', receipt `blocked`, `stop_reviewer` called once, `review.json` absent and no second launch on a further `drive`; add a variant that dirties `review-worktree` or rewrites `review.diff` before acceptance for the worktree/evidence checks, and one where `stop_reviewer` raises inside the except branch to cover the 'Could not confirm reviewer stop' event.

findings.title: Check and scenario ids the policy contract accepts are rejected by the adapter, taking the whole workflow listing down with RUN_STORAGE_INVALID
findings.file: server/projects.ts:94 and :99 (id = ID_PATTERN) vs contracts/workflow/verification.schema.json:50 and :62 ("minLength": 1 only); copied verbatim by workflow/export_state.py:124-126; same pattern in contracts/projects/v1.ts:103,108
findings.evidence: The producer-side policy contract (`contracts/workflow/verification.schema.json`, checks[].id and scenarios[].id) and `workflow/verification.py:validate_policy` accept any non-empty string; `inputs_section` copies the ids unchanged; the adapter's `workerInputSchema` and the projects contract require `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$`. Exercised with /tmp/claude-1000/-home-agentops-dev-md-manager-ultra/9ef1cac0-1832-43a8-bc1f-712f36914ef4/scratchpad/build_badid.py (legacy_run fixture, policy check id changed to `test:unit`, plan.policy_sha256 re-pinned, `validate_policy` passes, `export_run(ExportRuntime(...))` writes run-state.json 1.2.0) and drive_adapter.ts: `listRuns FAILED: 500 RUN_STORAGE_INVALID: Run "legacy-001" has malformed or contradictory persisted state: run-state.json inputs.workers.ui.checks.0.id: Invalid string: must match pattern /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$/`. A scenario id containing a space fails the same way (`inputs.workers.ui.checks.2.scenarios.0.id`). Because `RunStore.listRuns` (server/projects.ts:~585) projects every run and throws on the first invalid one, every run in that workflow disappears behind the 500, not just the offending run.
findings.failure:
policy.json with a check id such as `test:unit` (npm-script style) or a scenario id with a space/colon -> `workflow prepare`/`launch` accept it, the run executes and exports version 1.2.0 -> GET /api/projects/

/workflows//runs answers 500 RUN_STORAGE_INVALID for the whole workflow and the run detail/inputs/review routes for that run are unreachable.
findings.fix: Pick one side and make the other match: either tighten `contracts/workflow/verification.schema.json` (checks[].id and scenarios[].id `pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$`, so `prepare` refuses the policy before a run starts) or relax `workerInputSchema` in server/projects.ts:94,99 and `runInputWorkerSchema` in contracts/projects/v1.ts:103,108 to `z.string().min(1)` (the ids are never used as path or route components). Add a test on whichever side changes.

findings.title: Export invents `reviewer_transport: "native"` for plans pinned before the setting existed, contradicting the same export's `review.transport`
findings.file: workflow/export_state.py:141 (`automatic.get("reviewer_transport", "native")`); served unchanged by server/projects.ts:projectInputs (`automatic: { ...section.automatic }`); contract field non-nullable at contracts/projects/v1.ts:136
findings.evidence: export_state.py's own rule (lines 4-5: "Missing evidence is `null` ... never guessed") and PRD_RUN_INPUTS.md section 4 ("inputs are pinned per run from the run's own files") are violated for every automatic run whose plan.json predates `reviewer_transport`, which includes project-workflows-001 (the run HANDOFF_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md section 5 says to re-export after merge; its plan was pinned 14:33Z before the native reviewer existed and its review was print-mode). Exercised with build_runs.py variant `legacy` (legacy_run fixture: plan.automatic has four keys, automatic-review.json present, no review.interactive.json): the exported run-state.json carries `review.transport: "print"` and `inputs.automatic.reviewer_transport: "native"` at the same time, and the adapter serves both (`reviewResult` transport=print, `runInputs.automatic.reviewer_transport=native`). Note: DESIGN_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md section 2 explicitly sanctions this default ("reviewer_transport defaults to native when the plan predates it"), so this is a spec-level inconsistency rather than a deviation from the spec; `automatic.py:58-60` uses the same default for the controller's future behaviour, where it is harmless because such plans never launch a new reviewer.
findings.failure: Re-export project-workflows-001 (or any pre-slice-A automatic run) -> the Assignment tab and run header state the run was configured for a native reviewer while the review node of the same run states the reviewer transport was print; a reader cannot tell which is the recorded fact, and the value shown as a run input does not exist in the run's files.
findings.fix: Stop guessing in the export: when plan.automatic lacks the key, either emit the transport the run actually recorded (`"print"` when automatic-review.json exists without review.interactive.json, i.e. the same derivation review_section already uses) or make the field nullable end to end (contracts/projects/v1.ts:136 `reviewer_transport: z.enum([...]).nullable()`, regenerate runInputs.schema.json, adjust inputsSectionSchema in server/projects.ts:129 and the UI to render "not recorded"). Update DESIGN_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md section 2 accordingly and add a test_export case for a four-key plan.

findings.title: PRD_RUN_INPUTS §5 'findings grouped by worker' is not implemented and the deviation is unrecorded
findings.evidence: The UI deliverable row in PRD_RUN_INPUTS.md line 48 reads 'findings grouped by worker with requirement quotes that open the Task panel'. ReviewDetail.tsx builds `groups` only from DISPOSITIONS (line 101) and renders one <section data-disposition> per disposition (line 148); `worker` is a table column and a data-worker attribute, never a grouping. The design spec (§5.2) deliberately dropped the per-worker grouping, but neither docs/HANDOFF_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md §6 nor the PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY decisions log records that choice, and no scenario in inputs.spec.ts asserts a per-worker view.
findings.failure: A reader checking slice C against its PRD opens the review node of run-succeeded expecting findings grouped by worker (ui / adapter / both / none) and finds only Open/Resolved/Accepted sections with a Worker column; the PRD and handoff give no indication this was decided rather than missed.
findings.fix: Either add a per-worker grouping (or a toggle) to ReviewDetail.tsx, or record the decision (grouping by disposition with a Worker column, per-worker grouping dropped) in HANDOFF §6 and the umbrella decisions log and reword PRD_RUN_INPUTS.md line 48.

findings.title: Reviewer identity/independence re-check at acceptance has no test; fakes cannot reach that branch
findings.evidence: PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md §3 row 'Independence: reviewer UUID must differ from both worker UUIDs; verified from claude agents --json' and §4 item 5 ('rejected completion file … wrong UUID … fails closed') are implemented by `_accept_native`: `if row is None or row.get('sessionId') != receipt.get('session_id') or receipt.get('session_id') in worker_ids: raise RuntimeError('Reviewer identity changed or is not independent…')`. grep for 'not independent' / 'Reviewer identity' across workflow/test_*.py finds no test of this line. FakeSessions.locate returns the row whose sessionId equals the receipt's own session_id, and FakeSessions.REVIEWER_UUID never equals a worker id, so no automatic-graph test can trigger either condition. The existing tests cover the file's launch_token binding (test_completion_with_wrong_launch_token_fails_closed), locate's UUID drift (test_locate_reviewer_binds_the_review_worktree) and check_review's independence rule at export time, none of which asserts that a completion file is refused when the live reviewer row's UUID differs from the receipt or equals a worker's UUID.
findings.failure: A regression that drops or inverts the `receipt.get('session_id') in worker_ids` clause (or the row/receipt equality) would pass the whole Python suite while a completion file from a session that is not the launched, independent reviewer would be accepted.
findings.fix: Add a NativeReviewerGraphTests case that, after the fake reviewer writes its file, makes FakeSessions.inventory report the reviewer row with a different sessionId (and another case with the ui worker's session id as the reviewer id), then assert RuntimeError containing 'not independent', receipt status 'blocked', review.json absent and no relaunch on a second drive.

findings.title: Review node projects as pending (attempt 0, no session) while an interrupted native review is still running
findings.evidence: `_accept_native` emits `runtime.event('review', 'interrupted', …)` on KeyboardInterrupt and leaves automatic-review.json at `running` (tested by test_interrupted_reviewer_wait_keeps_the_reviewer_and_resumes_in_a_new_process). The adapter's EVENT_STATUS maps only running/interactive/blocked/succeeded/passed/approved; `interrupted` (and `stopped`) map to null. In projectSnapshot the review node has no task error, no interrupt and no `values.review` in that window, so `eventStatus` is null and line 879 assigns 'pending'; line 881 then forces attempt 0, session_id null, result_uri null. The reviewer's earlier `running`/`interactive` events are overridden because lastEvent (line 825-830) keeps the last raw event regardless of whether its status is mapped. This reintroduces exactly the symptom the umbrella PRD §1 names ('the viewer cannot show … the reviewer') for the interruption path that slice A's §5 acceptance bullet 3 makes a first-class state, and features/project-workflows/README.md's claim that raw event statuses map onto graph nodes does not hold for the new reviewer statuses.
findings.failure: Operator Ctrl-Cs the supervisor during the review (RUNBOOK 'Interruption' bullet), opens the run in the viewer: the review node reads 'Pending' / 'Graph attempt 0 (not started)' / 'No session recorded' although workflow-<run>-reviewer is alive in `claude agents --json` and automatic-review.json says `running`.
findings.fix: Map the new reviewer statuses in EVENT_STATUS (`interrupted` → 'paused' or 'running', `stopped` → null but do not let it override an earlier mapped status), or make lastEvent track the last event with a mapped status; add a server test with events [review/running, review/interactive, review/interrupted] and no review section asserting the node is not 'pending'.

findings.title: RUNBOOK claims `attach` adds the reviewer pane to an existing run, but attach_panels refuses whenever terminals.json exists
findings.evidence: RUNBOOK line 188: '… `attach-one --node review` reconnects in any available terminal, and `attach` adds the pane when the reviewer already exists.' `attach_panels` (interactive.py:291-292) raises 'Terminal mappings already exist; use attach-one inside an available terminal to reconnect' whenever `<run>/terminals.json` exists, which is the normal state of every run that `launch` attached (the worker panes are created at start). The reviewer branch at line 331 is only reached on a first attach. `attach_reviewer_panel` (line 358), the function that actually adds a third pane to an existing tab, is called only from Pipeline.launch_reviewer and has no CLI action (interactive.main choices: prepare, run, status, attach, attach-one).
findings.failure: The controller logs 'Reviewer pane not attached: <reason>' (pipeline.py launch_reviewer best-effort path, e.g. HERDR_ENV unset in the controller or a transient Herdr error). Following the RUNBOOK the operator runs `python -m workflow.interactive attach "$RUN"` and gets 'Terminal mappings already exist…'; there is no documented way to create the reviewer pane in the run's tab, only attach-one inside a pane they create by hand.
findings.fix: Either expose `attach_reviewer_panel` as an action (e.g. `attach-reviewer`) and reference it in the RUNBOOK, or make `attach` add the reviewer pane when terminals.json has ui/adapter but no review entry; otherwise reword RUNBOOK line 188 to say `attach` only creates the reviewer pane on a first attach.

findings.title: PRD_REVIEWER_PANE §3 says the completion file is bound to the reviewer session UUID; the schema binds a controller launch_token and the deviation is unrecorded
findings.evidence: PRD table row line 26: 'Bound to | run id, `review` node, bundle SHA-256, candidate commit, reviewer session UUID'. The schema's required keys (line 7) are version, run_id, node_id, launch_token, bundle_sha256, candidate_commit, verdict, findings; there is no session field, and `read_review_completion` binds `item['launch_token'] == receipt.get('launch_token')` where launch_token is `str(uuid.uuid4())` minted by `_review_native` before the session exists. The session UUID is verified separately from `claude agents --json` (automatic.py:298-301). RUNBOOK and contracts/workflow/README.md describe launch_token, but the PRD row was left as written and HANDOFF §6 / the PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY decisions log do not record the substitution.
findings.failure: An auditor cross-checking review.completion.json against PRD_REVIEWER_PANE §3 finds no reviewer session UUID in the file and no recorded decision explaining that binding to the session identity happens out of band via the launch receipt; the PRD's own 'Bound to' row is false as a description of the artefact.
findings.fix: Record in HANDOFF §6 (and the umbrella decisions log) that the file binds a controller-issued launch_token because the session UUID does not exist when the prompt is composed, with the session identity enforced from the launch receipt at acceptance; update the PRD table row accordingly.

findings.title: Vacuous assertion for launcher invocations in worker-inputs scenario
findings.evidence: `await expect(launch).toContainText('1')` is meant to check the "Launcher invocations" fact, but the same `launch-receipt` panel already contains the timestamps "2026-03-01 10:00:00 UTC" / "2026-03-01 10:00:02 UTC" (asserted on lines 144-145), so any text containing a "1" satisfies it.
findings.failure: If `LaunchReceipt` (src/projects/WorkerInputs.tsx:141) rendered `launcher_invocations` as `undefined`, `NaN`, or dropped the row entirely, this assertion still passes; the scenario claims coverage of the launch receipt fields it does not actually verify.
findings.fix: Assert the specific definition item, e.g. `await expect(launch.locator('dt:has-text("Launcher invocations") + dd')).toHaveText('1')`, and likewise pin the observed-state row instead of `toContainText('done')`.

findings.title: "Diff the reviewer saw" link trusts diff.uri after a prefix-only check, unlike every other scoped route
findings.evidence: `diffScoped` is only `review.diff.uri.startsWith(`${paths.run(scope)}/artifacts/`)` and line 133 renders `<a href={review.diff.uri} target="_blank">`. The contract's `artifactSchema.uri` is `z.string().min(1)` (contracts/workflow/v1.ts:14), so the remainder is unconstrained and `artifact_id` is never cross-checked against the URI. The rest of the viewer is segment-strict (`scopedResultPath` api.ts:174-180, `scopedReviewPath` api.ts:197-202) and `WorkerEvidence` never trusts `uri` at all: `ScreenshotArtifact`/`TextArtifact` rebuild the URL from `artifact_id` via `paths.artifact(scope, id)` (NodeDetail.tsx:48, 72).
findings.failure: A review payload whose `diff.uri` is `/api/projects/p/workflows/w/runs/r/artifacts/../../other-run/artifacts/x` (or `.../artifacts/x?y`, or a uri whose last segment differs from `artifact_id`) passes the prefix test, renders as a scoped link, and the browser normalises it to another run's (or a foreign) route when clicked; the module's stated invariant "artifacts and results are only ever requested through the scoped routes of the run being viewed" (api.ts:6) is not enforced for this link.
findings.fix: Build the href from the id, as the evidence panels do: `paths.artifact(scope, review.diff.artifact_id)`, and treat `review.diff.uri !== paths.artifact(scope, review.diff.artifact_id)` as the unscoped state (the same single-segment rule `scopedResultPath` applies).

findings.title: Finding link is derived from the raw task text while the highlight searches the served text, so a link can land on "nothing is highlighted"
findings.evidence: `FindingRow` renders `finding-task-link` whenever `requirement_found_in` names a lane (lines 71-88) and never consults the served task it already has via `inputs`. The adapter computes `requirement_found_in` on the RAW, unbounded task/prompt text (server/projects.ts:387-395, design spec §2), but `TaskPanel` locates the quote with `text.indexOf(activeQuote)` on `worker.task.text` (WorkerInputs.tsx:43), which is `redactPaths`-ed and cut at 65536 characters with a marker (server/projects.ts:370-377); the miss is only surfaced after navigation by the `task-highlight-missing` note (WorkerInputs.tsx:59-61).
findings.failure: A worker task longer than 65536 characters with the quoted requirement after the cut (or a quote whose leading path redacts differently from its context in the task, e.g. `**/home/x/y**` where `*` is not in the redaction lookbehind set): the review node shows "Open in the ui task" as a verbatim match, clicking it navigates to launch_ui, forces the Source view, and shows "The quoted requirement was not found in this task text, so nothing is highlighted" — contradicting PRD_RUN_INPUTS §1/§6 ("clicking a finding's requirement quote opens that worker's task scrolled to the quote") and the `finding-task-unlinked` promise that unlinked quotes are the only ones that don't resolve.
findings.fix: In `FindingRow`, when the lane's inputs are loaded, only render the link if `worker.task.text.includes(finding.requirement)` (fall back to the `finding-task-unlinked` note, or a variant noting truncation when `worker.task.truncated`); alternatively have the adapter compute `requirement_found_in` against the served (redacted, bounded) text so the flag means what the viewer uses it for.

findings.title: Post-wait reviewer identity/independence re-check is untested and unfalsifiable with FakeSessions
findings.evidence: Mutation on a scratch copy: deleted the four lines in `_accept_native` (`row = runtime.sessions.locate(...)`, `worker_ids = ...`, `if row is None or row.get("sessionId") != receipt.get("session_id") or receipt.get("session_id") in worker_ids: raise RuntimeError("Reviewer identity changed or is not independent; refusing the verdict")`) and ran NativeReviewerGraphTests + AutomaticGraphTests + ReviewCompletionTests: 18/18 pass. No test file references "identity changed or"/"not independent" (grep). FakeSessions.inventory builds every row from the receipts on disk with the constant REVIEWER_UUID, and locate matches on that same receipt session_id, so no graph test can ever make the live row differ from the receipt or equal a worker UUID. PRD_REVIEWER_PANE §3 table ("Independence: reviewer UUID must differ from both worker UUIDs; verified from claude agents --json"), design spec §3.3 ("re-check reviewer identity (locate row sessionId == receipt session_id and not equal to either worker session id)") and HANDOFF §1 ("identity/independence/worktree/evidence re-checks") all claim this check.
findings.failure: Reviewer session swapped or hijacked between writing review.completion.json and the controller's poll (row sessionId != receipt session_id), or a worker session id reused as the reviewer: with the check removed the verdict is accepted. For a blocked verdict `_decide` writes review.json before any independence check, so a non-independent blocked review is persisted; for an approved verdict only check_review's receipt-vs-bundle comparison remains, never the live `claude agents --json` row. No test turns red for any of this.
findings.fix: Add knobs to FakeSessions (e.g. `reviewer_row_session_id` override and `reviewer_vanishes_after_file`) so a NativeReviewerGraphTests case can make locate("review") return a different UUID, a worker UUID from the bundle snapshots, or None after the completion file exists; assert RuntimeError "identity changed or is not independent", receipt status blocked, stop_reviewer called once, no review.json, second drive does not relaunch.

findings.title: Worktree-unchanged and evidence-unchanged re-checks after the reviewer wait have no test (native or print)
findings.evidence: Mutation on a scratch copy: deleted `if git(cwd, "rev-parse", "HEAD") != bundle["candidate_commit"] or git(cwd, "status", "--porcelain"): raise RuntimeError("Reviewer worktree changed")` and `if runtime.validate_bundle()[1] != digest or digest_file(patch) != receipt["patch_sha256"]: raise RuntimeError("Evidence changed during review")` from `_accept_native`; NativeReviewerGraphTests + AutomaticGraphTests 14/14 pass. `git show HEAD:workflow/test_automatic.py | grep` shows these strings were never tested in the print path either; HANDOFF §1 and §4 present them as part of the native accept path with "behavioural reds per increment".
findings.failure: review.diff rewritten or review-worktree dirtied/moved to another commit while the reviewer runs (e.g. an operator resumes the transcript and edits): the completion file is still accepted and review.json/automatic-review.json record `succeeded` against evidence the reviewer did not see; no test detects the missing guard.
findings.fix: Reuse the `reviewer_mutate` hook style: a FakeSessions callback invoked in run_reviewer after writing the completion file that (a) touches a file inside `<run>/review-worktree`, (b) rewrites review.diff; assert the exact RuntimeError message, receipt blocked, stop called, review.json absent.

findings.title: Print-mode recording of finding `worker`/`requirement` is untested: the fake print reviewer always returns `findings: []`
findings.evidence: Mutation on a scratch copy: changed REVIEW_SCHEMA finding `required` to `["severity", "message", "disposition"]` and removed the `worker`/`requirement` properties; PrintReviewerGraphTests + CompletionTests 18/18 pass. The fake print executable prints `"structured_output": {"verdict": verdict, "findings": []}` in every test, so the extended schema and the `worker`/`requirement` values never reach review.json or the export's `review.findings` in print mode. HANDOFF §1 claims `_review_print` is "now also recording worker/requirement"; design spec §3.3 says both are required in REVIEW_SCHEMA.
findings.failure: REVIEW_SCHEMA regresses (fields dropped or made optional, or enum widened to accept e.g. "reviewer"): print-mode reviews persist findings without the link fields, the export's `review.findings[].worker/requirement` are null, and slice C's finding-to-task links silently never appear for print-mode runs. All Python tests stay green.
findings.fix: Make the fake executable read an optional findings JSON file (like `review-verdict`) and add a PrintReviewerGraphTests case that supplies a finding with worker/requirement and asserts review.json and run-state.json carry them; add a negative case (finding without `worker`) asserting "Reviewer did not succeed"/schema failure and receipt blocked.

findings.title: "A missing pane never fails the review" and the reviewer launch-failure receipt (`needs_reconciliation`) have no test
findings.evidence: Mutation on a scratch copy: (a) in Pipeline.launch_reviewer removed the try/except so a failing attach_reviewer_panel propagates (guard `terminals.json` + HERDR_ENV==1 kept); (b) in `_review_native` replaced the `except BaseException as error: receipt.update(status="needs_reconciliation", error=...); save_json(...); raise` with a bare re-raise. Ran workflow.test_automatic, test_interactive, test_export, test_feature_launch: 73/73 pass. grep of the test files for "Reviewer pane" and "needs_reconciliation" finds only the worker/interactive receipt cases, none for the review node. PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY decisions log: "a missing pane never fails the review (slice A)"; HANDOFF §1: "launch_reviewer (events with the reviewer UUID, best-effort pane)" and "automatic-review.json ... needs_reconciliation" on launch failure.
findings.failure: (a) Under Herdr with terminals.json present, a pane allocation error (pane occupied, Herdr RPC failure) raises out of the review node: the run fails after the reviewer session was already launched, and no offline test notices the lost best-effort guarantee. (b) A `claude --bg` launch that times out or exits non-zero leaves automatic-review.json at `launching` with no error string; the RUNBOOK's reconciliation guidance keyed on `needs_reconciliation` does not apply and no test asserts the status.
findings.fix: Unit test on Pipeline.launch_reviewer with a SimpleNamespace sessions whose run_reviewer returns a receipt, terminals.json present, `patch.dict(os.environ, {"HERDR_ENV": "1"})`, and `patch("workflow.pipeline.attach_reviewer_panel", side_effect=RuntimeError(...))`: assert the receipt is returned and an event "Reviewer pane not attached" exists. Graph test with `patch.object(f.runtime, "launch_reviewer", side_effect=RuntimeError)`: assert automatic-review.json status `needs_reconciliation` with the error, no review.interactive.json/review.json, and that a second drive raises without calling run_reviewer.
